The Problem

An emergency doesn't happen in a perfect system.

Most emergency response logic quietly assumes the person can respond, communication exists, GPS is available, the device has battery, and infrastructure remains up. Guardian is built around what happens when one or more of those assumptions stop holding.

The person may become unable to manage the emergency at exactly the moment the system requires human interaction. At the same time, communication, location, sensing and device resources may also degrade. What happens next is the question Guardian is built to answer.

System Architecture

The sensors are the evidence. The innovation is the decision pathway.

Eight stages, one continuous loop. Select a block to see what it does and why it exists.

Persistent Emergency State

One record, held and updated through the whole event.

Rather than a single alert, Guardian maintains a structured record of the emergency: what's known, what's degraded, what's been tried, and what's still viable. It persists across failures instead of resetting with each one.

emergency_state.jsonIllustrative
Human Agency

Guardian evaluates whether a person appears able to respond — not whether it "knows" they can't.

Guardian does not claim to know a person is unconscious or incapacitated. It evaluates observable interaction against a small set of agency states, and treats reduced agency as a factor in its decisions — not a diagnosis.

RESPONSIVEResponsive

The person interacted with the app or device in a way consistent with awareness — dismissing a countdown, confirming safety, or speaking.

UNCONFIRMEDUnconfirmed

No interaction has been observed yet, but the window for expected response has not elapsed.

NON-RESPONSIVENon-responsive

Expected interaction did not occur within the window, and no alternative signal indicates awareness.

UNKNOWNUnknown

Insufficient evidence exists to place the person in any of the above states.

Emergency Viability Engine

The question is not just "what happened?"
The question is "what response is still viable?"

Guardian weighs human agency, communication availability, location confidence, device resources, available sensing, relay opportunities and prior outcomes to choose among candidate actions — not to compute a single provably-optimal score.

current_state

cellularUNAVAILABLE
batteryLOW
relayAVAILABLE
AKeep retrying cellular
BContinue expensive GPS acquisition
CPreserve emergency state + use relay
DReduce all activity
RATIONALE

Cellular unavailable. Battery constrained. Relay available. Direct retry deferred to preserve emergency communication capability.

Guardian selects an action according to a defined policy over these factors. Where the underlying evaluation is not implemented as a precise numerical optimization, the site does not present one.

Current Verdict

Guardian does not guarantee a transmission pathway will exist. When no viable pathway remains, the emergency state is preserved for recovery rather than discarded.

Location Continuity Research Direction

When GPS disappears, location shouldn't become meaningless.

Guardian maintains the best available location estimate and its uncertainty when conventional positioning becomes unavailable, rather than dropping location entirely. This does not imply reliable indoor positioning.

GPS available → GPS location
GPS unavailable → PDR / inertial estimation
Independent evidence available → Fuse / correct
No reliable estimate → Last reliable location + uncertainty
Connectivity restored → Synchronize
Multilingual Communication Accessibility Layer

Localized wording. Controlled data.

Structured fields — risk, timestamp, location, response status — remain controlled and unambiguous. Only the human-readable explanatory text is localized, currently in English, Hindi and Urdu.

Healthcare

Emergency response is part of healthcare.

The period between an emergency and professional care can be disrupted by loss of human agency, communication, location, information or device resources. Guardian sits in this pre-hospital window.

Infrastructure Disruption

Personal emergency continuity when infrastructure is down.

Guardian does not replace disaster-response agencies. It aims to preserve a personal emergency's context and continuity while cellular, internet, GPS and device resources are degraded.

Security & Privacy

Collect less. Expose less. Retain less.

Emergency data is sensitive. Critical decisions should not depend on cloud AI availability; AI in Guardian is assistive, not authoritative.

Current Prototype
  • Minimized emergency data collection
  • Assistive, non-authoritative AI role
  • Scoped access to trusted-contact data
Production Requirements
  • Stronger authentication
  • Encryption and key management
  • Strict database access rules
  • Logging and retention policies
  • Independent security testing

Guardian does not claim to be "completely secure" or "impossible to compromise."

Credibility

What Guardian knows — and doesn't.

Guardian can know
  • Sensor evidence
  • Event timing
  • Risk estimate
  • User interaction state
  • Location estimate and confidence
  • Communication availability
  • Resource state
  • Previous action outcomes
Guardian does not automatically know
  • Whether the user is definitely unconscious
  • Whether every message is guaranteed delivered
  • Whether GPS is always accurate
  • Whether arbitrary nearby phones can relay
  • Whether an emergency service has actually arrived
  • Whether a medical condition is correctly inferred

Alignment

Two failure contexts, one adaptive architecture.

Guardian applies to personal healthcare emergencies and to disaster / infrastructure disruption — the same architecture, different sources of failure.

Personal emergency
Reduced human agency
Infrastructure / capability failure
Adaptive response
Continuity
The person can fail. The sensor can fail. The location can fail. The network can fail. The device can fail. The response should not stop trying to adapt.

"Guardian is not built on the assumption that everything will work. It is built to adapt when something doesn't."

Safety shouldn't stop when its assumptions do.
